notes:
Segment states-tn-kl-py covers Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry in full except districts (owned by local-lgd).
As-of 2026-09-25. All three had assembly elections Apr-May 2026 and each saw a change of ruling party/CM:
- Tamil Nadu: TVK (actor Vijay's new party, founded Feb 2024) became the single largest party (108/234) and Vijay
  became CM on 10 May 2026 in coalition with INC/IUML/VCK, ending decades of DMK-AIADMK alternation. No Deputy CM.
- Kerala: UDF (INC-led) won a landslide (102/140), ending two LDF terms; V. D. Satheesan (INC) became CM 18 May 2026.
- Puducherry: incumbent N. Rangasamy (AINRC) and the NDA alliance were RE-ELECTED, his fifth term as CM (13 May 2026).

Research constraints and honest gaps (severity noted):
1. WebSearch tool quota was exhausted session-wide before this segment's research began (shared budget across
   parallel research agents); all research after that point relied on WebFetch (single-pass, AI-summarized) of
   Wikipedia pages plus a handful of direct Wikipedia API/HTML fetches via curl. No official state-portal (tn.gov.in,
   kerala.gov.in, py.gov.in) cabinet pages, PIB releases or news-site cross-checks were possible — only Wikipedia.
   Confidence is capped at "medium" for anything that rests on a single WebFetch summary rather than a primary
   document, even where the underlying Wikipedia article looks well-sourced.
2. Full council-of-minister lists (TN 34 of a reported "35 total" ministers, Kerala 20, Puducherry 5) come from a
   single WebFetch pass each over the "<CM> ministry" Wikipedia article; portfolio splits, exact swearing-in dates
   for individual ministers, and minister Wikipedia links were NOT individually cross-verified. TN source claimed
   "35 total" ministers but the rendered table only named 34 — the missing one could not be identified, so only 34
   are recorded (do not treat 34 as necessarily exhaustive).
3. Deputy CMs: none of the three states currently show a Deputy Chief Minister in the sources found. Not asserting
   there is none — only that none was found.
4. Chief Secretary / DGP are civil-service appointments that can change independent of the election cycle and were
   the hardest to verify: TN Chief Secretary (M. Sai Kumar) is cross-verified from two sources (medium-high
   confidence); TN DGP (Sandeep Rai Rathore) was an ECI-appointed neutral DGP for the April 2026 poll — whether he
   continued post-election is unverified (confidence low). Kerala Chief Secretary is reported to have changed from
   A. Jayathilak to Bishwanath Sinha around July 2026 but no dedicated source could confirm this independently
   (confidence low). Kerala DGP and Puducherry DGP could not be found in the sources available and are recorded as
   positions with holder=null rather than invented (confidence low). Puducherry Chief Secretary (Sharat Chauhan) has
   one source only.
5. Tamil Nadu State Human Rights Commission: existence/legal basis recorded, but no current chairperson could be
   confirmed (article not found under expected title) — holder omitted.
6. Kerala State Human Rights Commission: same gap as above, even less confirmable — entity recorded without a
   headPositionId or holder.
7. Puducherry: it has no Lokayukta (explicitly excluded, along with J&K, under Indian practice) and — as far as
   could be verified — no distinct State Election Commission or State Public Service Commission separate from
   Union-level machinery; these were therefore NOT created as entities rather than guessed. Puducherry also has no
   ULB formally elevated to "municipal corporation" status; the five municipalities (Puducherry, Oulgaret, Karaikal,
   Mahe, Yanam) are recorded under kind "municipal_corporation" per the schema's closed kind list for this segment's
   local-body layer, with a note in each description clarifying their actual (lower) legal tier — flag this if the
   schema is later extended with a "municipality" kind.
8. Puducherry assembly party-wise strength: the election-result page and the assembly-composition page disagree
   slightly on AINRC's exact seat count (12 vs 11) once the 3 nominated members and post-poll realignment are
   folated in; both figures are given with a note rather than silently picking one.
9. No Legislative Council exists in any of TN, Kerala or Puducherry (correctly out of scope per the task brief,
   which lists only UP/Bihar/Maharashtra/Karnataka/AP/Telangana as having one).
10. Municipal-corporation mayors were not verified for either state (Wikipedia list pages did not carry current
    mayor names) and are therefore omitted rather than guessed, per the task's "mayor only if easily verifiable"
    instruction.
11. Governor of Tamil Nadu: Kerala's Governor (Rajendra Arlekar) holds ADDITIONAL CHARGE of Tamil Nadu since 12
    March 2026 (no dedicated full-time TN Governor as of the as-of date) — flagged with "acting": true on the
    holder rather than treated as a routine appointment; worth re-checking as this is an unusual, likely temporary
    arrangement.

--- ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION PASS (2026-09-25) ---
Re-checked with fresh 2025-2026 sources (Wikipedia via WebFetch/curl API; WebSearch was session-wide exhausted, same constraint the original research hit). Corrections applied are listed in the top-level 'verification' block. Remaining known gaps not fixed in this pass (kept low-confidence / omitted rather than invented): TN DGP post-election continuation still unconfirmed; Kerala Chief Secretary transition (A. Jayathilak -> Bishwanath Sinha) still single-source; TN/KL State Human Rights Commission chairpersons still unconfirmed; exact per-minister swearing-in dates for the 2 (of 5) Puducherry ministers sworn in 13 May 2026 vs the 3 sworn in 17 June 2026 could not be individually attributed, so all 5 keep the 5 Aug 2026 portfolio-allocation date with an explanatory note, as in the original file. Also flagged: this segment has no 'indirectly_elects' relations from st-tn-assembly/st-kl-assembly/st-py-assembly to individual Rajya Sabha member positions (owned by the parliament-* segment) as suggested by the task brief -- adding those needs coordination with parliament-rajya-sabha.json's exact position IDs and was out of scope for this verification pass.
